summary: Proceed as one run with no companions. The change is a shape-gated kwarg flip on the w13 Marlin call at T=1, so the bs=1 row is the only readout. The expected gain is about 0.9 us of 44 us (z about 1.5 in the prior run), roughly 0.3% on the headline, so treat it as the run that closes the w13-atomic knob rather than as a likely promotion.
justification: Mechanism: at T=1 with block_size_m=8, w13 has about 4 m-blocks x 64 n-tiles. The prior run's slice estimate gave about 2 split-K slices per CTA. Atomic add replaces the fp32 global-reduce pass between those slices, which plausibly saves a microsecond or two on a launch-bound kernel (Marlin pair 42.1 us against a 11.4 us floor). At T>=8 the estimate falls to 1 slice, so atomic buys nothing there, which fits narrowing the gate to T=1. The prior evidence (job 171684977ec1470f, w13 atomic at T<=32 on master 9080a71) is bs=1 44.02 vs 44.88 us with err_ns 573. That is about 1.5 sigma, inside the +/-1.5% the judge calls noise. Weakest link: the profiled Marlin pair read 34.2 vs 42.1 us (-7.9 us), but end-to-end moved only 0.86 us. Either the profile comes from a different job and harness (BEST's 42.1 is from 7a0d900a, not a paired run) or most of the profiled saving is hidden in launch/graph overhead. Do not cite the 8 us as the expected effect. The bs=8 'recovery' half of the bet cannot be measured: the prior bs=8 row (107.8 vs 106.0) was already flat within noise, so going back to master at T=2..32 can only read flat. The headline CI (+/-1.5%) cannot resolve a ~0.3% headline change. Read only the bs=1 row and its Marlin top_kernels entry against the paired master runs. Expected directions match TASK's equal load weights (60 each, geomean over loads).
confounders: w2-marlin-atomic-add-small-m (landed, same knob on the second Marlin call, same T=1 path): w13's output feeds silu_and_mul and then w2-atomic. The self-check gate is measured against w2-atomic master (T=1 rel-L2 0.00788 vs tol 1e-2). If w2 were not atomic, the w13 timing would not change (separate launch), but the correctness margin would. Timing confounding is negligible, numeric coupling only.

marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm / triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack: these fix block_size_m=8 and the sorted_ids layout at T=1, which set m_blocks and therefore the split-K slice count that atomic add acts on. They are shape-fixed and unchanged by this hypothesis, so they set the operating point but do not confound the A/B.

align-parallel-per-expert-verify, post-expert-norm-triton-small-m, sglang-marlin-path-parity: these share the launch sequence at T=1 (align, then post-norm combine) but touch neither the w13 kernel nor its memory traffic. No confounding.
interference: No companion. An ab-revert of w2-marlin-atomic-add-small-m would change the bs=1 baseline by about the same 1-us magnitude as the effect, adding noise rather than resolving it. A control has nothing to isolate, because the change is a single kwarg flip. The real ambiguity is statistical: a 2% effect at a 1.3% per-shape error. A second identical run is deduped, and a companion would not help. With moe at 5 checks left and 5 queued, the check is better spent elsewhere. If bs=1 reads flat or slower, close the w13 atomic knob as the hypothesis says. If it reads faster by >=1 us again, that is two independent same-direction readings and enough to submit-test.
rules_flags: None blocking. kernel_fn adds only a host-side branch on num_tokens (a shape, not a value) and a different kwarg, which is graph-capturable with no sync. The self-check and its try/except stay in prepare.

Note: keep the T=1 self-check gate at W13_ATOMIC_TOL=1e-2. The measured T=1 rel-L2 vs master was 0.00788 with a fixed seed. Atomic-add ordering is nondeterministic, so a rerun could read slightly higher, and a fallback to master would make the run measure nothing. The log must print PATH CHOSEN so a master fallback is harvested as VOID. Error against the FP32 reference stays well under 1.5% (the prior run passed 5/5).

Drop the prior run's print-only _marlin_exec_config_probe (graph captures, 320 MB flush buffer, explicit thread_k/thread_n configs). It is not part of this change, it costs prepare-time budget, and it carries the residual sticky-fault risk the previous audit flagged. The `change` paragraph keeps only the self-check, so the builder should not copy the probe.
open_questions: Was the Marlin pair 34.2 us (hyp) vs 42.1 us (master) measured under the same profiler and graph mode? If master's paired profile also shows about 34 us, the profile-level 'gain' is a harness artifact and the prior is weaker than stated.

Does Marlin's atomic path zero C internally? The prior self-check passed 'atomic' (no memset) with poisoned output buffers at T=1/4/8, which suggests yes. The w2 atomic write into cache3 aliases cache1, so the builder should keep the poison test to catch a regression there.
